hook.evidence: Motivates leveraging foundation models and multi-modal data for wireless prediction/control.

gap.evidence: Notes absence of surveys covering multi-modal FMs for wireless prediction/control and development/deployment issues.

yes_but.evidence: Acknowledges related surveys but highlights missing comprehensive FM-in-wireless view.

contribution.evidence: Lists contributions including multi-modal applications, prediction/control roles, datasets, methods, and open issues.

scope_boundary.evidence: Scope includes FM background, multi-modal context understanding, prediction, control, datasets, methods, and open issues.

rhetorical_moves_global.reader_contract_pattern: Motivate FMs for wireless; review FM background; survey multi-modal applications; cover prediction/control roles; discuss datasets and methods; list open issues; conclude.

visuals_tables.layout_logic: Figures/tables illustrate FM applications, datasets, and method comparisons; open issues are text-heavy.

figures.purpose: depict FM roles in multi-modal wireless prediction/control

tables.purpose: summarize datasets or FM method comparisons

lesson_blocks.lesson: FMs extend wireless context understanding across vision, graph, 3D, and other modalities.
Traffic and other predictions benefit from FM generalization.
FMs can supervise RL or act as agents, but integration remains early-stage.
Wireless-specific datasets and tailored pre-train/fine-tune/inference methods are critical for FM performance.
Future work needs modality-specific FMs, knowledge infusion, deployment strategies, security/robustness, on-device models, latency control, data scarcity solutions, and agentic AI.

synthesis.aha_moment: Organizing FM-in-wireless by modality, task (prediction/control), and development resources clarifies how FMs can be systematically adapted and where gaps remain.

style.section_openers_pattern: Introduce FM role/domain then enumerate subtopics with figures/tables; frequent lists.
